The role combines HR expertise with operational coordination and strategic people management to support a productive, professional, and well-structured organization. The position involves managing key areas of the employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, employee records, performance management, engagement, development, compensation, and workplace policies. You will work closely with employees and managers to ensure that HR processes are consistent, efficient, and aligned with organizational priorities. Key responsibilities include coordinating recruitment activities, supporting workforce planning, preparing employment documentation, maintaining accurate employee information, and ensuring that onboarding and employee administration processes are completed effectively. The HR & Administration Manager component involves overseeing day-to-day HR and administrative operations. You will coordinate workplace procedures, internal documentation, office-related processes, employee services, and administrative resources while ensuring that organizational standards are maintained. The role also focuses on employee engagement and workplace culture. You will support initiatives that strengthen communication, collaboration, employee satisfaction, recognition, and organizational alignment. You may coordinate employee events, engagement activities, internal communications, and feedback processes. Performance management is an important responsibility. You will support managers in establishing objectives, conducting performance reviews, addressing performance concerns, and identifying opportunities for employee development. You will also contribute to talent management, succession planning, and organizational capability initiatives. At the CPO level, the role provides strategic people leadership and works closely with senior executives to develop workforce strategies that support business growth and organizational transformation. You will assess workforce requirements, organizational structures, leadership needs, and people-related risks. The position requires monitoring HR metrics and workforce data, including recruitment activity, employee turnover, engagement, workforce costs, attendance, and other relevant indicators. These insights will support management decisions and continuous improvement of HR programs. You will also help develop and maintain HR policies, procedures, employee guidelines, and administrative frameworks. The role requires awareness of applicable employment requirements and a commitment to fair, consistent, and professional workplace practices. The position may involve managing HR teams, administrative staff, external service providers, recruitment partners, and other stakeholders. You will establish priorities, coordinate activities, and promote accountability and service quality. The role also supports organizational change, including restructuring, transformation initiatives, leadership changes, and the implementation of new people processes or systems. Strong communication and stakeholder management are essential when guiding employees through organizational changes. Success in this role requires strong interpersonal skills, confidentiality, leadership, organization, strategic thinking, and sound judgment. You should be capable of balancing employee needs, operational requirements, and broader organizational objectives. Strong understanding of HR operations, talent management, employee relations, recruitment, and organizational development. Strong recruitment, workforce planning, onboarding, and employee engagement capabilities. Excellent interpersonal, communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills. Strong understanding of performance management, talent development, succession planning, and organizational culture. Ability to work effectively with employees, managers, senior leadership, and external stakeholders. Strong employee-relations and conflict-resolution skills. Ability to handle confidential employee information with discretion and professionalism. Strong organizational and administrative management capabilities. Ability to analyze HR data, workforce metrics, and organizational trends. Familiarity with HRIS, payroll platforms, applicant tracking systems, performance management tools, and other HR technologies. Strong project management and process improvement skills. Ability to manage multiple HR and administrative priorities simultaneously. Understanding of compensation, benefits, workforce budgeting, and employee-related costs. Ability to support organizational change, transformation, restructuring, and culture initiatives. Strong leadership and team-management capabilities. Excellent reporting, presentation, and documentation skills. Strong business awareness and ability to connect people strategies with organizational objectives. Professional HR qualifications or certifications are considered an advantage. High level of integrity, accountability, confidentiality, and professional judgment. A people-focused, strategic, commercially aware, proactive, and results-oriented approach to HR leadership.
